cohort: A total of 156 pregnant women who delivered at term without comorbidities were included from two geographically distinct regions of Turkiye: Istanbul (sea level) and Agri (moderate altitude).
finding: Neonates born at moderate altitude had significantly lower birth weights and birth weight percentiles compared to those born at sea level, independent of maternal comorbidities, suggesting altitude impacts fetal growth.
cross-section timing: Data was collected at term delivery for neonatal outcomes, and for maternal first-trimester hemoglobin and hematocrit levels.
birth_weight: Mean birth weights were 3117 +/- 424 g for the high-altitude group and 3351 +/- 402 g for the low-altitude group.
